question.text: An existing LP in Yamuna Venture Fund (Cat I VC) wants to sell its secondary interest. The fund's reported NAV attributable to this LP's units is INR 40 crore. Market secondary transactions for Indian VC funds of this vintage typically clear at an 18% discount to NAV. What is the approximate effective price the exiting LP would realise?

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook p.294 supports secondary transactions at negotiated prices, often at a substantial discount to NAV. Using the stem's 18% discount: effective price = NAV x (1 - discount) = INR 40 crore x 0.82 = INR 32.80 crore, matching keyed option A. The Trap: INR 40 crore ignores the discount. INR 47.20 crore applies the discount as a premium (wrong sign). INR 28.80 crore over-discounts by treating 18% as a 28% haircut (40 x 0.72). Note: Removed the discount-sensitivity modelling and future-drawdown-collapse pro-tip together with the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, since those negotiation specifics go beyond the secondaries discussion on p.294.
